document.title: Afghanistan: Russian Embassy Official Claims Iran Interfering more than Pakistan (Islama 11049)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] A Russian Embassy official says Pakistan gives the Taliban modest financial assistance, logistics, fuel and military training and ignores a booming smuggling trade. He says Taliban funding mostly comes from Afghan traders and that Pakistani aid is smaller than Iranian aid to the Rabbani government.

events.description: Zamir Kabulov briefed US embassy officer on Russian perceptions of Pakistani and Iranian involvement in Afghanistan
Cable sent from Embassy Islamabad to State Department
Russian diplomat Zamir Kabulov briefed U.S. Embassy political officer on Pakistani and Iranian involvement in Afghanistan.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cabled State Department reporting Kabulov's claims that Iran interferes more than Pakistan.
Iran allegedly established an air bridge from Mashhad to Baghram with several nightly flights carrying weapons and money; Turkmenistan protested privately.
Pakistan trained 20-30 Taliban in tank and artillery in Quetta and gave refresher flight training to ex-Najibullah pilots.
Taliban captured weapons at Shindand and Herat and were besieging Kabul.

key_claims: Per Kabulov, most Taliban funding still came from Afghan traders, with modest Pakistani government money to key figures in the Kandahar Central Shura.
Kabulov alleged Pakistan supplied jet and diesel fuel, communications gear and radar repair to the Taliban.
Kabulov alleged ISID gave only small amounts of ammunition, since the Taliban captured enough at Shindand and Herat.
Pakistan allegedly trained 20-30 Taliban in tank and artillery in Quetta and gave refresher flight training to ex-Najibullah pilots.
Kabulov claimed Iranian support for the Rabbani government far exceeded Pakistani aid to the Taliban, including bribes to Dostam, Khalili and Hekmatyar.
Iran allegedly trained several thousand anti-Taliban Afghan refugees and ran night flights from Mashhad to Baghram, prompting a Turkmen protest.
Kabulov admitted aid from the former Soviet Union to Rabbani and Masood was probably increasing.
